summary: A list of the ICP sockets for accessing UCSB's online graphics from supported terminals and protocols, including IMLAC terminals with special software, Tektronix terminals and systems supporting the proposed Level 0 graphics protocol. It names a contact for questions.

eli5.summary: A directory telling which door number to knock on for each kind of drawing screen, so the school's drawing service can talk to it.

subtitle: Directory of socket addresses for UCSB online graphics services

tldr.problem: UCSB had several graphics protocols available on the network, but users needed to know which socket (ICP address) to connect to for each type of terminal.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC lists five socket addresses that support different graphics terminals and protocols: IMLAC with standard software, IMLAC with 80x80 display grid, Level 0 graphics protocol, and TEKTRONIX terminals.
tldr.outcome: The socket list made it easy for remote users to access UCSB's graphics capabilities using whatever terminal hardware they had.

today: RFC 398 is classified as Unknown status. It documented a specific graphics service available on UCSB's network systems in 1972.

sections.title: UCSB Graphics on the Network
sections.content: UCSB provided online graphics services to ARPANET users. Users with TEKTRONIX or IMLAC display terminals, or systems supporting the Level 0 graphics protocol, could access UCSB graphics. The RFC lists the ICP (Initial Connection Port) socket addresses for each supported terminal type, with contact information for detailed questions.
sections.eli5: UCSB has drawing machines you can use from your terminal over the network. This tells you which address to connect to for your type of machine.

sections.title: Supported Terminal Types
sections.content: The RFC documents five socket configurations. IMLAC terminals with special software designed by Jerry Powell send graphics over a simplex connection and alphanumerics over a TELNET-like connection. Another socket serves IMLAC terminals with an 80x80 display grid and standard text editing (though some IMLACs had 64x64 grids). TEKTRONIX terminals including models 4002-A, 4010, and T-4002 were tested successfully, and the system expected all other 4002-compatible terminals to work.
sections.eli5: Different drawing screens need different connections. Some have fancy keyboards built in, some share a text connection, and some are tested with TEKTRONIX machines.

sections.title: Formatting Challenges
sections.content: A primary problem encountered by users centered on display formatting. The system lacked terminal-independent positioning for alphanumeric output because only one terminal type had been in house during design. Programs that drew and labeled graphs neatly on one terminal might not display properly on others. Efforts were underway to provide at least minimal device independence, and users were encouraged to contact John Pickens, Glen Davis, or Mark Krilonovich with suggestions and criticisms.
sections.eli5: Text labels sometimes appear in the wrong spot on different screens because the system was built for only one type. The team is working on making it better.
